scope: 6xm integer grid, q=7 (7 co-circular or 7 co-linear forbidden stones), width-6 seed of the fixed-width occupancy program

six_x13_crosscheck.note: chord census = independent brute-force circumcenter census, identical circle sets

row_span_distribution.note: unlike 5x19 where every 8-point census circle spans exactly 4 rows, width-6 census circles span 4, 5 or 6 rows

claims.census: For every tested m in {13,16,19,22,25,28,31,34,40,46,52,58,64,70}, the 6xm grid contains exactly census_6xm[m].total circles with >=7 lattice points; all of them have exactly 7 or 8 points; no circle with >=9 lattice points exists in any 6xm grid with tested m<=70. The only >=7-point lines are the 6 row lines (a non-horizontal line meets 6 rows in <=6 points).
claims.witnesses: For each m in {19,25,31,40,46,52,58} a full-capacity (6,6,6,6,6,6) 36-stone safe maximal configuration exists (rows listed; column-mirror canonical form). Safety is verified by two independent exact-integer paths (danger-census check and stone-triple circumcircle enumeration); maximality is a proof: each row holds exactly 6 stones and m>=7, so adding any stone creates 7 collinear stones on its row.
claims.scope: Finite computed facts. These do not determine M_{6,7} (the smallest m at which every maximal safe configuration on 6xm is full-capacity); that requires the deficient-row-class enumeration campaign.

density_observation: random full-capacity configurations are safe with rate 147/200 (m=19) rising to ~200/200 (m>=46): violations become rarer as m grows at fixed 36 stones
